scenarios.title: NPC corporate buy must pay and settle in native GameStore
steps: Give verified NPC corporation wallet, shortage, and docked Rust ask
Authorize buy through eventual native corporate buyer authority
Restart buyer after lost RPC ACK
expected: Debited ISK equals credited ISK and market fees, exact amount
One physical stack changes owner once
No phantom shipment or repeated purchase

scenarios.title: Partial buy remains disabled without atomic splitter
steps: Place native Rust sell stack 100 while buyer needs 10
Issue buy request without native splitter
expected: No partial transaction, no phantom items or ISK

scenarios.title: Real fill-backed repricing respects bounded spread
steps: Create genuine native trade fills at station
Change verified stock and observed demand
Evaluate price quote and place native order with same source custody
expected: Price changes only within strict safety limit
Price stays above verified material+fee floor
No speculative price pump without native fill provenance

scenarios.title: Zero-ISK NPC self-recovery sells existing output
steps: Set corporate wallet to verified zero and preserve already-paid physical stock
Complete native sale to a real player and verify corporate credit
expected: Listing and READY delivery remain allowed at zero cash
No new paid manufacture or buy without verified cash

scenarios.title: Regional production profit uses actual supply and buyers
steps: Provide two region-specific SDE recipes, real BPO and verified order/fill volumes
Measure material, production, freight and market costs
Choose profitable product and observe physical transport
expected: No simulated buyer or artificial turnover
Transport and material costs paid in native accounting

scenarios.title: Cross-corp and wrong-station asks cannot feed buyer
steps: Create two corporations with their own station wallets
Include foreign-owned or duplicate Rust order in buyer snapshot
Attempt intent planning and native authorization
expected: No wallet charge or incorrect stock transfer
Player orders and corp custody remain isolated
